about: Somebody Get These Beggars Outta Here is a close-up of Robert Pattinson as Antinous in Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, grinning wide in a dim, firelit hall. Antinous leads the suitors who have taken over Odysseus's home, and his line dismissing beggars drips with the confidence of someone who thinks he is untouchable. As a meme it is used to wave away things that ask for attention: messages, notifications, requests, rivals or lowball offers. There is a built-in irony fans enjoy too, since in the epic the beggar in the hall is the disguised Odysseus about to take his revenge.
origin: The line is from Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, released in July 2026, with Robert Pattinson as the suitor Antinous. Clips of his smug delivery spread across social media within days of release.
usage:
Put the thing being dismissed in the top box: recruiters, cheap offers, a phone low-battery warning, other teams in the league. The bottom box carries the line itself, "somebody get these beggars outta here".

The more arrogant the dismissal the better, so it fits rich-guy energy, ranked-match trash talk, and anyone ignoring obvious warnings. For extra irony, make the "beggar" something that will clearly come back to bite you, just like in the story.
